evidence.source: Shuowen.org, reproducing Shuowen and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.field: definition; component analysis; cited textual examples
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry defines 睡 as 坐寐 (“sleep while sitting”) and analyzes it as 从目、垂. Duan Yucai cites Zuozhuan 坐而假寐 and Zhanguo ce 讀書欲睡, and says a Song edition lacks 聲; his explanation links 目 to drooping eyelids. This is a historical account and later commentary, not direct evidence of an early physical graph or the date of surviving witnesses.
evidence.title: 說文解字「睡」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A02792 睡: Shuowen analysis and senses/examples
evidence.text: The entry reports the Shuowen gloss 坐寐也 and lists 睡 in the Shiji example for falling asleep while seated; Zhuangzi and Hanshu examples glossed as sleeping; and a Rulin Waishi example glossed as lie down. These are separate transmitted-text attestations, not proof of a chronological semantic chain or manuscript dates.
evidence.title: A02792 睡 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00764 垂: Shuowen graphic and phonetic analysis; variant notes
evidence.text: The entry reports Shuowen’s analysis of 垂 as 从土 with a phonetic element. It also documents nonstandard and variant forms of 垂, including one described as a vulgar error. This supports the sound-component analysis of 垂 itself and variation in its transmission; it does not show that 睡 is corrupt or that the same variant occurs in 睡.
evidence.title: A00764 垂 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: No securely dated excavated 睡 graph was verified. The searched Qin manuscript database covers many forms, but its overview does not show a specific 睡 entry; the earliest physical graph and detailed graphic evolution remain unresolved.

The Shuowen gloss and cited classical examples attest lexical framing in transmitted texts, while the MOE entry distinguishes seated sleep, sleep, and lying down. Dates of surviving witnesses and semantic links or chronology among these senses remain unestablished.
No evidence located that 睡 is a whole-graph phonetic loan or that 睡 itself is corrupt. The documented variant and error notes concern 垂 forms and cannot be transferred to the host graph.

Local exact kMandarin rows for 目, 垂, and 睡 and Baxter–Sagart rows for 垂 and 睡 were checked from the supplied data. The direct official Unihan character pages were inaccessible; the Baxter–Sagart PDF surfaced exact row text in search but its opened page failed with 502.
The Commons file is only a modern Shuowen-style drawing lead, not an ancient artifact. Its page, image pixels, and API metadata could not be verified; no glyph image is selected or recommended.
No versioned local text extract is recommended: no inspected evidence established reuse terms for bulk dictionary text, and the character-specific claims can be checked from the cited pages.
